\section[o julgamento]{o julgamento — the trial; the judgement}

\label{lesson:PT-C390-julgamento}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the sanction, then the Portuguese for to fine.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o julgamento}
\textbf{o julgamento} — \textquotedblleft{}the trial; the judgement\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O julgamento começa na segunda-feira.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The trial starts on Monday.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Ir a julgamento} — to go on trial.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{julgamento} is built on \emph{julgar} \textquotedblleft{}to judge\textquotedblright{} with \emph{-mento}; \emph{julgar} is inherited from Latin \emph{iūdicāre} \textquotedblleft{}to judge\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), on \emph{iūdex} \textquotedblleft{}judge\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o julgamento}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o julgamento}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{o julgamento}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the sanction, then the Portuguese for to fine, then say \emph{o julgamento} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does o julgamento mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The trial; the judgement\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[testemunhar]{testemunhar — to testify, to bear witness; to witness}

\label{lesson:PT-C390-testemunhar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to fine, then the Portuguese for the trial.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: testemunhar}
\textbf{testemunhar} — \textquotedblleft{}to testify, to bear witness; to witness\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ela testemunhou a favor do arguido.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{She testified for the defendant.}
\end{quote}

Also to witness an event: \emph{testemunhar um acidente}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{testemunhar} is built on \emph{testemunha} \textquotedblleft{}witness\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{testimōnium} \textquotedblleft{}evidence, testimony\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{testis} \textquotedblleft{}witness\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{testemunhar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to fine, then the Portuguese for the trial, then say \emph{testemunhar} again

\section[a culpa]{a culpa — the blame, the fault; the guilt}

\label{lesson:PT-C390-culpa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the trial, then the Portuguese for to testify.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a culpa}
\textbf{a culpa} — \textquotedblleft{}the blame, the fault; the guilt\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A culpa não foi tua.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{It was not your fault.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Ter a culpa} — to be to blame; \emph{por culpa de} — because of.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{culpa} comes straight from Latin \emph{culpa} \textquotedblleft{}fault, blame\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short), with no change of form.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the trial, then the Portuguese for to testify, then say \emph{a culpa} again
\end{itemize}

\section[culpado]{culpado — guilty; to blame}

\label{lesson:PT-C390-culpado}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to testify, then the Portuguese for the blame.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: culpado}
\textbf{culpado} — \textquotedblleft{}guilty; to blame\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O juiz considerou-o culpado.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The judge found him guilty.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Considerar culpado} — to find guilty.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{culpado} is the participle of \emph{culpar} \textquotedblleft{}to blame\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{culpa} \textquotedblleft{}fault\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{culpa} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[inocente]{inocente — innocent}

\label{lesson:PT-C390-inocente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the blame, then the Portuguese for guilty.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: inocente}
\textbf{inocente} — \textquotedblleft{}innocent\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ele diz que está inocente.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He says he is innocent.}
\end{quote}

Also naive: \emph{uma pergunta inocente}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{inocente} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{innocēns} \textquotedblleft{}harmless, blameless\textquotedblright{}, built from \emph{in-} \textquotedblleft{}not\textquotedblright{} and \emph{nocēre} \textquotedblleft{}to harm\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inocente}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inocente}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{inocente}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the blame, then the Portuguese for guilty, then say \emph{inocente} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[(dialogue)]{Revisão dos capítulos 383–390}

(\textbf{válido}.) To expire? (\textbf{caducar}.) To run out? (\textbf{expirar}.) To renew? (\textbf{renovar}.) The certificate? (\textbf{o certificado}.) The bureaucracy? (\textbf{a burocracia}.) The accusation? (\textbf{a acusação}.) Lawful? (\textbf{lícito}.) Unlawful? (\textbf{ilícito}.) The complaint? (\textbf{a queixa}.) The accused? (\textbf{o arguido}.) The witness? (\textbf{a testemunha}.) The defence? (\textbf{a defesa}.) The court sentence? (\textbf{a sentença}.) To punish? (\textbf{punir}.) The penalty? (\textbf{a pena}.) The prison? (\textbf{a prisão}.) The conviction? (\textbf{a condenação}.) The punishment? (\textbf{o castigo}.) The crime? (\textbf{o crime}.) The criminal? (\textbf{o criminoso}.) The corruption? (\textbf{a corrupção}.) The sanction? (\textbf{a sanção}.) To fine? (\textbf{multar}.) The trial? (\textbf{o julgamento}.) To testify? (\textbf{testemunhar}.) The blame? (\textbf{a culpa}.) Guilty? (\textbf{culpado}.)
